voyage.name: Museo Municipal de Arte Contemporáneo
voyage.content: In the Municipal Palace at Plaza Regocijo, this museum has exhibitions of contemporary art. Admission with the boleto turistico

voyage.name: Museo Histórico Regional
voyage.content: In the home of the Inca historian Garcilaso de la Vega, this 2-story museum has many paintings from the 17th and 18th century as well as historical displays chronicling the pre-Hispanic Inca civilization, the invasion of the Spanish and the role of Christianity in the post-conquest era. A tour is unlikely to take much more than an hour.

voyage.name: Machu Picchu Museum
voyage.price: Foreigners S/20, international students and Peruvians with ID S/10, Peruvian students S/5
voyage.content: The largest collection of Machu Picchu artifacts in the world. These artifacts were collected by Yale University researcher Hiram Bingham beginning in 1912 and returned to Peru in 2011. The museum is housed in a late 18th-century house called Casa Concha.

voyage.name: Museo del Centro de Textiles Tradicionales de Cusco
voyage.content: A beautiful (and free) museum inside El Centro's textile store, featuring a gallery containing displays of traditional Quechuan and Andean textiles. The museum explains the historical significance of textiles and the techniques by which they are made. A must-see, and visitors can buy the traditional textiles as they come in. A large majority of the money goes to the women who produce them, and the textiles are of muc

voyage.name: Museo del Sitio del Qoricancha
voyage.content: With information about the different pre-Columbian cultures and fragments of ceramics and textiles of the Inca culture. A very small museum, the showcase room includes three mummies and skulls modified by the Incas with holes or sloped foreheads. Allow an hour to an hour and a half. English explanations are present but lacking.

voyage.name: Museo de Arte Popular
voyage.content: Displays a collection of popular art featuring handcrafts of the modern era.

voyage.name: Santa Catalina Convent
voyage.alt: Monasterio de Santa Catalina de Nuestra Señora de Los Remedios
voyage.content: Also a collection of religious art. Admission with the boleto turistico.

voyage.name: Qoricancha
voyage.content: The central site of worship for the Incas. Like so many other testimonies of fantastic Inca architecture, it was severely devastated by the conquistadores, the Spanish conquerors, who built their Christian church, Santo Domingo, on top of the ruins. Yet most of the bottom part of the temple is fairly well preserved and makes the site worth several hours of your time. The site is one of the best in Cuzco, containing b

voyage.name: ChocoMuseo
voyage.content: A shop ("museum") explaining the history of cacao (free) and offering chocolate workshops (not free) as well as cacao farm tours (not free). Different recipes from around the world are available all made with chocolate from the factory inside the cacao and chocolate museum. Great artisanal and organically sourced hot chocolate.

voyage.name: Museo Inka
voyage.content: Extensive museum of pre-Inca, Inca, and colonial artifacts. Labels in English and Spanish, though the descriptions in English are sometimes pretty different from the ones in Spanish.

voyage.name: Piedra de los doce ángulos
voyage.content: A large stone in one wall has 12 sides and 12 angles. This one has become almost a symbol of Cusco and is a striking example of the precision of Inca architecture and stonework.

voyage.name: Monumento Pachacuteq
voyage.content: Down Av. Sol, is a statue of the Inca warrior King Pachacuteq. The statue is placed on a cylindrical base and the total monument is over 22 m high. The cylindrical base can be climbed, but views are disappointing because the monument is in a lower part of town.

voyage.name: Cusco Cathedral
voyage.alt: Catedral Basílica de la Virgen de la Asunción
voyage.content: Elaborate large cathedral full of colonial-era religious paintings. The biggest church in Cuzco, in front of Plaza de Armas. As a tourist the entrance is S/25. If you go in a "misa" (mass) between 06:30–09:00, it is free. No photography allowed.

voyage.name: Palacio Inka del Kusikancha
voyage.alt: Dirección Desconcentrada de Cultura de Cusco
voyage.price: No admission fee, but the attendant who lets you in and shows you where to go expects a S/5 tip
voyage.content: The ruins of an Inca palace, the home of 15th-century Inca emperor Pachakuti Inka Yupanki, which you can walk around in. The Inca and colonial stonework and architecture is interesting.

voyage.name: Plaza de Armas
voyage.content: The park square has churches, shops, restaurants and bars surrounding it, and is a great place to spend an afternoon. The historical center of Cuzco is beautiful, but you will have to deal with all the street vendors and hawkers of cheap paintings and other souvenirs. They are everywhere in and around the Plaza de Armas. They somewhat spoil the experience.

voyage.name: Plaza de San Francisco,
voyage.content: A great place to visit one of Cuzco's many great coffee shops. Next to the Plaza is the main market, which is fairly traditional and is a worthwhile visit. The market has a mix of stalls selling food and other household items as well as clothing and souvenirs.

voyage.name: Salseros Cusco
voyage.content: Take a Salsa class, or three. This is a fabulous little salsa school offering private and group classes at minimal price in two central locations. With enthusiastic teachers and a number of styles taught, this is the perfect time to polish your moves and get ready to shine on the dance floor. Ask for Franshesco Efernetti if you want private classes.

voyage.name: Planetario Cuzco
voyage.content: Information about Inka astronomy, projection and explanation of the southern sky in the dome, observing stars, planets and other objects with telescopes.

voyage.name: Sacsayhuamán
voyage.content: The closest and largest of these ruins is the amazing Sacsayhuamán (sometimes called Saqsaywaman and pronounced "Sock-say-wah-mun"), the ruins of an Inca fortress high above Cuzco. It is a steep climb from the Plaza de Armas up Plateros street which changes to Saphi. Look for the long staircase on the right, follow the paved curvy road up to the next cobblestone pedestrian path and follow this climb past the first cl

voyage.name: Qenko
voyage.content: The second site up the road from Sacsayhuamán. Take the combi shared buses up the hill for S/1 or take a walk of about 0.5–1 km up a gradual incline to visit the site. Its name means "Zig-Zag" in Quechua, and probably refers to the Zig-Zag channels carved into a rock. Explore the pass through cave and view the altar on which llamas were sacrificed. The large erect stone shown on the boleto turistico is a solar calend

voyage.name: Pukapukara
voyage.content: Named after the red hue of the hillsides nearby. The third site along the route, even heartier walkers will find the walk a bit long and a bit steep despite the paved and well traveled road. However, the views along the walk are great and small mud brick bars are intermittent between the sites. Hire a taxi or take a combi shared bus up from Qenko for S/1 to save time and energy. A larger site than Q'enqo, the guides

voyage.name: Tambomachay
voyage.content: The most distant ruin on the route from Cuzco. It is a small site with an ornamental fountain whose source is unknown as reportedly archaeologists lack the tools necessary to determine the source without damaging the site. Likely it is an underground spring. In several Incan sites such as Ollentaytambo water sources were covered or underground to protect the water supply from poisoning. Accessible with the boleto tur

voyage.name: Cochahuasi Animal Sanctuary
voyage.content: A one-of-a-kind rehabilitation center started by a family of biologists, which provides shelter to animals injured or victimized by poaching. It's a happy place where animals get better and those able are re-released. In 2012, there were three condors, llamas, alpacas, vicunas, macaws, pumas, an unusual furless Peruvian dog, local deer, all very friendly. This is the best place to see pumas, condors and vicunas up cl

voyage.name: Rainbow Mountain
voyage.price: from US$25 including breakfast, lunch and entrance fee
voyage.content: A challenging early-morning, high-altitude hike to a beautiful multicolored mountain. Tours usually start around 04:00 with a breakfast break near or in Cusipata at around 07:00. Now there's a new path leading to the mountain from the west, the former 3-hour hike (from the east) is more a 90-minute walk now. Horses can be hired for a fee, children with llamas or sheep offer to pose for a photo (free/included in the e

voyage.name: Mercado San Pedro
voyage.content: The largest market close to the center. Though it's becoming more tourist-oriented it still has plenty of genuine local colour, a nice change from Plaza de Armas. If you're looking for a full blown market with a special aisle for entrails, this is the place to be. Colorful, vibrant, packed, San Pedro Market is not to be missed. You can find all manner of fruits, vegetables, cheeses, chocolates, honey, meats, househol

voyage.name: Casa Ecologica
voyage.content: Good for fair-trade textiles.

voyage.name: T'Ankar Gallery
voyage.content: Good for well-made but pricey indigenous weavings and pottery. No obvious fakes or tourist junk.

voyage.name: Mercado de San Blas
voyage.content: A lovely place to enjoy a delicious breakfast before starting a journey. Handcrafts available as well as fruits, vegetables and grocery items.

voyage.name: Artisan Market
voyage.content: If you don't want to go so far away, but still want touristy stuff, go to the big red building near the fountain. Also try the main market by Plaza San Francisco. This market is almost exclusively tourist-oriented goods. There are a few restaurants inside as well.

voyage.name: Centro Comercial El Molino, Urbanizacion Ttio
voyage.content: Another market, you have to take a taxi and it costs S/2 to get there. In this market you can buy pirated merchandise including DVDs and CDs. A good quality copy DVD is S/3. Be aware that DVDs here may be region-encoded for region 4. These will not play on many DVD players purchased in the U.S. or Canada. Look for DVDs encoded for region 0, or you can see about modifying your DVD player to accept all DVDs.

voyage.name: Los Angeles
voyage.content: For late night food after clubbing, a very good fast food-type restaurant.

voyage.name: Chifa Status
voyage.content: Good quality Chifa. Dishes for S/2-3. Ample portions invite sharing. Credit cards accepted.

voyage.name: El Encuentro
voyage.content: Reasonably priced vegetarian restaurant with good portions. The S/10 dinner includes soup, main course and mate. Free salads with lunch. They also do soy meat very well. There are two of these restaurants but the one in Calle Tigre near Plaza de Armas is S/8 for exactly the same menu.

voyage.name: El Fogon
voyage.content: Nothing fancy but great cheap food: for S/10 you get a meal deal that includes a plate from the salad bar, a selection of soup, a selection of main dish, a dessert and a beverage. Or splurge with their more expensive menu offer for S/20. Very tasty Peruvian food. Friendly staff.

voyage.name: Victor Victoria
voyage.content: Friendly service. Great salad bar buffet included in all main dishes. Gorgeous garlic trout with rice or potatoes for S/10 (including the salad bar buffet and lovely fresh bread) but only for lunch. Great value breakfasts. Regular glasses of freshly squeezed juice for S/6. Also they have a proper espresso machine for good coffee in the morning.

voyage.name: Chia Vegan Kitchen
voyage.content: Arguably the best vegan place in Cusco, and very good value for money. Looks good, smells good, tastes good, and the staff is super friendly. Lunchtime offer includes drink and salad buffet for S/15. À la carte dishes are more expensive, but worth it. If you're up for a hot drink and/or something sweet, try the enormous hot chocolate for the (very enjoyable) sugar shock of the day.

voyage.name: Bagdad Cafe
voyage.content: This small restaurant seems to produce everything themselves. Local food is extremely good, in the evening small performance groups enter the restaurant and give excellent performances. The prices are mid-range, but it is sure worth it. The daily menu lunch special is more like a snack.

voyage.name: Jack's Cafe
voyage.content: This is a great place to get a big breakfast complete with eggs, bacon, avocado, toast and fantastic thick shakes. Very popular with tourists. Try the homemade lemonades. Right outside of Jack's is an empanada stand which has great rocoto salsa, a spicy salsa that goes well on the cheese or meat-stuffed pastries.

voyage.name: Cicciolinia
voyage.content: This is a very tasty place to go for breakfast. Another location, Cicciolinia Café, is on Ruinas, which is open from 7:00 AM and good for brunch.

voyage.name: Emperador
voyage.content: They have a 13-page menu with all sorts of foods from around the world. Try the pisco sour tall.

voyage.name: Encantasq'a
voyage.content: A nice place to have a break with coffee and a snack. Especially the chocolate cupcakes are delicious and make up for half a lunch. They also have fresh cakes, quiches and juices.

voyage.name: Green Point
voyage.content: Vegan restaurant popular with tourists, serving breakfast, lunch, and dinner. Various international dishes, and some Peruvian food. Gluten-free and raw options. Menu in English and Spanish. Wifi available.

voyage.name: Inka Grill
voyage.content: Well-known and frequented by tourists but not a trap. Excellent food. Good place to try cuy (guinea pig); some people have reported mud butt after eating it, it is tastily done and served without the head so eating doesn't remind you of your pet hamster. Try the appetizer tiradito de trucha. Alpaca also on the menu.

voyage.name: Restaurant Inkazuela
voyage.price: Appetizers around S/15, mains around S/28
voyage.content: This place specializes in stews. Food is delicious and friendly waitresses will take good care of you. Well chosen music and a fireplace create a romantic atmosphere.

voyage.name: Tunupa
voyage.content: They offer some of the best guinea pig or alpaca dishes from the local Novo Andino cuisine as well as other local specialties, including cuy; it's served here without the head (but with the feet).

voyage.name: Morena Peruvian Kitchen
voyage.content: Peruvian classics in an upscale setting on the Plaza de Armas. Reservations highly recommended months in advance during the high season. Walk-in wait times can be >2 hours during peak meal times.

voyage.name: Gato's Market
voyage.content: Small and a bit pricey.

voyage.name: La Canasta
voyage.content: Well-stocked.

voyage.name: Mega
voyage.content: This is the largest supermarket in Cuzco.

voyage.name: Mama Africa
voyage.content: On three levels. Snacks, a cafe on the rooftop, restaurant with a good cheap menu, two discos, the latest movies on DVD. Some of the decorations and paintings are by the owner/artist. Lots of people, good music, good atmosphere and free salsa lessons. Salsa starts at about 21:00 and goes until about 23:00. If you really want to learn some moves, dance with Carlos, Miguel, or Checo, who work there. It also plays host

voyage.name: El Muki
voyage.content: A place with more locals than the Plaza de Armas. It has a unique cave-like interior and is one of the city's oldest discos.

voyage.name: Caos
voyage.content: If you want to get away from the tourist crowd for a while and dance the night away with the locals, head to this very nice large club with a great mix of music and exotic drinks.

voyage.name: Paddy's Irish Pub
voyage.content: The night-brother of Jack's Cafe. Not exactly traditional Peruvian fare, but an excellent atmosphere among fellow travellers in a cozy upstairs pub setting. Purportedly the highest 'Irish-owned' pub in the world at 3,400 m, it offers a good selection of pub food (think cottage pie, casseroles, mash and gravy), local and international drinks (even had cider and Guinness), and a useful "No Gracias" T-shirt for sale.

voyage.name: Mythology
voyage.content: Disco that offers salsa. If you want to learn Rueda Cubana, this is the place to go. Classes usually start around 21:00 and private lessons can be arranged with Cesar, the dance instructor. Mythology also offers a unique decor of gods and goddesses and has the cleanest restrooms of all of the nightclubs, by far.

voyage.name: Ukuku's
voyage.content: Live music with local and traveling artists playing a variety of different music styles including salsa, meringue, criolla, and Afro-Peruvian. There are great decorative masks in the walls and a huge wooden woman statue with butterfly wings.

voyage.name: Los Perros
voyage.content: Chill restaurant/lounge. Ethnic food and comfortable couches. Has a variety of their own locally brewed house beers.

voyage.name: Le Nomade
voyage.content: 2nd floor, cnr of Choquechaca and Cuesta San Blas 207. Coffee bar/lounge with live music every night. Reggae, Latin, cubano, afro-Jazz, blues, bossa, funk, soul, rock and española. No cover. Friendly staff.

voyage.name: The Lost City Roasters
voyage.content: Small basement bar one block from the plaza de Armas. Very friendly place to watch American football or basketball and chat to the regulars and owners. Great pizzas and paninis, cheap happy hour cocktails and beers. A real bar for locals, expats and Cusqueños.

voyage.name: Organika Bakery y Cafe
voyage.content: Modern, bright coffee shop serving hot and cold coffees brewed via chemex, french press, or Japanese sifon. Offers coffee drinks with alcohol. Sandwiches made with homemade breads.

voyage.name: Three Monkeys
voyage.content: A coffee lover's coffee shop where you can specify the kind of bean you want for your coffee, roast level, and method of extraction (from basic drip to french press or cold brew). Uninviting barebones interior, but good coffee anyway.

voyage.name: Hospedaje Amanecer
voyage.content: A quiet place, private bathrooms, TV, wi-fi, hot shower.

voyage.name: Hostal El Arcano
voyage.content: A great little hostal overlooking the city with a variety of comfortable, affordable rooms.

voyage.name: Pisko and Soul
voyage.address: Calle Carmen Alto 294, San Blas District
voyage.content: Really nice for a hostel. Very friendly staff. Hot water, continental breakfast, free wifi. It's a new establishment so some books may not have it listed especially if the print is a few years old.

voyage.name: Hospedaje El Artesano de San Blas
voyage.content: Well-kept place with good-value rooms around a colonial courtyard, hot water, common kitchen, helpful staff, wifi.

voyage.name: Taita Home
voyage.content: Dormitory beds in a freaky, chilled out and friendly atmosphere with a sunny garden, fireplace, outdoor kitchen and gas hot water.

voyage.name: Hostels Cusco Samanapata
voyage.content: Hostel in San Blas area of Cuzco, about 3 blocks from Plaza de Armas. Free wifi, 2 free computers, free breakfast, all rooms have cable TV. Very friendly staff, rooms cleaned daily. Much cheaper than similar places.

voyage.name: La Casa de mi Abuelo
voyage.content: A guesthouse near the Plaza de San Francisco run by a kind local lady that offers extremely clean and comfortable rooms, ensuite bathrooms, cable TV, and excellent breakfasts. 7-minute walk to Plaza de Armas

voyage.name: Pirwa Hostel Colonial Cusco
voyage.content: 24-hr hot showers, movies, in-house bar, pool (game) table, attentive staff, free breakfast, free internet, pick up service, and comfortable beds.

voyage.name: Pirwa Bed&Breakfast Posada del Corregidor Cusco
voyage.content: Movies, safe and relaxed environment, traditional meals, good view of the main plaza.

voyage.name: Hogar Clinica San Juan de Dios
voyage.content: Private and double rooms and windows that look onto the mountain range. Good service and daily egg breakfast. Non-profit hostel supporting the children's hospital next door.

voyage.name: Pariwana Hostel Cusco
voyage.content: Two blocks from the Plaza, hot showers, common areas are decorated with local designs, safe, clean.

voyage.name: Flying Dog Hostel
voyage.content: Great hostel with a wide range of rooms. Free wifi (in lobby, not room), breakfast, lockers, and coffee and tea all day. Check out their bar, and ask them to arrange tours for you. Friendly staff.

voyage.name: Hospedaje Estrellita
voyage.content: Shared double rooms surround a large concrete courtyard. There is a kitchen with a sociable commonroom with cableTV. A night cost S/15 and includes a small breakfast. It's popular with gringos.

voyage.name: Loki Cusco
voyage.content: 180 beds, noisy party hostel in a 450-year-old Peruvian national monument. Dorms from US$13, basic breakfast included. Wifi, tea and coffee are included. Hot water with pressure in generally shared showers. 13:00 checkout and small lockers in reception that have plug sockets in them.

voyage.name: Saqray Hostel
voyage.content: Has very beautiful rooms with private or shared bathroom and two small dorms. The place has a nice patio with a fireplace, it's completely clean and there is another sitting room with TV and cable and a computer with free internet on which to burn your own CDs or DVDs. Free wifi, laundry service, breakfast available. 2 blocks from the main square, close to the centre of 'fiesta'. Pressurized hot water available aroun

voyage.name: Casona Rimacpampa
voyage.content: Close to the plaza. Amazingly hot showers, with good water pressure. TV, food available.

voyage.name: Welcome Cusco Hostal
voyage.address: Asociacion San marcos A-3, San Blas
voyage.content: Free internet and wifi throughout, hot showers, towels available, and warm bed available. Use of kitchen. Only 6 blocks from the main square.

voyage.name: Hospedaje Corona Real
voyage.content: Quiet and cheap option about 15-min walk from the city center. Rooms are spacious and have private bathroom and local television and cost S/15 per person.

voyage.name: Cusco Central Hostel
voyage.content: Old world nostalgia with breakfast. No internet.

voyage.name: Hostal Mirador De San Blas
voyage.content: Breakfast, cable TV, wifi, friendly staff. Large rooms some with desks and refrigerator. Posted prices are high, but they can be talked down to S/45 per night.

voyage.name: Mirador del Inka
voyage.content: Very big but nice place in a historic building with great view over the city. Free wifi, breakfast optional. They also run a tour agency and tend to be very pushy in trying to sell their tours (which are very pricey, so try to haggle the price down!). Advertised price is US$30 for a nice double, but in the low season it was possible to lower it to US$15 (May 2012). Rooms on the upper floors are much better than the l

voyage.name: The Grasshopper Hostel
voyage.content: A relaxed backpacker hostel with dorms, private rooms and a super friendly staff.

voyage.name: VIP House Garden Hostel
voyage.content: One of the cheaper hostels in the city, but surprisingly nice. Wifi, free breakfast, inexpensive dinners available some days, bonfires in the evening, and a view of the city from the upstairs kitchen/dining room. (The affiliated VIP House Hostel is around the corner.)

voyage.name: Amaru Hostal I
voyage.content: Quiet and cheap option about 3 blocks from the Plaza de Armas. Rooms are decent sized and have private or shared bath facilities and TV. US$30–55/room depending on type of beds, occupancy and season.

voyage.name: Amaru Colonial Hotel
voyage.content: Quiet and cheap option about 2-3 blocks from the Plaza de Armas. US$30–48/room depending on type of beds, occupancy and season.

voyage.name: El Balcón Cusco Hotel
voyage.content: Awesome interior design, delicious breakfast and moderate prices. From Plaza de Armas, follow Plateros a block and a half or so. The hotel is in a lane up the hill. About half a block up, look for the door on the right. The sign is above the door, so you may not see it unless you walk on the opposite side of the lane.

voyage.name: Hostal Frankenstein
voyage.content: Clean, friendly and helpful German chef, a lazy iguana, creative interior, cosy atmosphere. Double costs around US$20 (the one on top is quiet and offers a view of Ausangate mountain).

voyage.name: Orquidea del Cusco
voyage.content: The colonial building has original Inca walls and exposed wood beams, and the rustic accommodations are simply decorated in a cozy mountain lodge aesthetic. All rooms are oriented toward Cuzco below, offering panoramic views.

voyage.name: Ninos Hotel Meloc
voyage.content: Hotel with charitable purposes: all procedures from room booking and in-house restaurant go towards running an association that gives support to local unprivileged children.

voyage.name: Gran Hostal Machu Picchu
voyage.content: Comfortable rooms set around a courtyard filled with lush plants.

voyage.name: Hostal Rumi Punku
voyage.content: Rumi Punku means "stone door" in Quechua: the entrance to the hotel leads through an ancient stone door, obviously of Inca design. The doorway is all that has survived of an Inca palace. The door is considered a historic item by the city of Cuzco.

voyage.name: Casa San Blas Boutique Inn
voyage.content: In the historic artisan's quarter 2½ blocks from the main square in a neighborhood of narrow, cobbled streets and whitewashed colonial-era houses. Friendly staff. US$110 a night for a single.

voyage.name: Koyllur Hostal
voyage.content: Richly decorated and a nice place to splash out for a few nights. Big buffet breakfasts. Ask for room at top floor in the front - has skylights, lots of room, nice furnishings. Cable TV, wifi.

voyage.name: La Posada del Viajero
voyage.content: Free Wi-Fi, 2 blocks from Plaza de Armas, breakfast, hot water, kitchen.

voyage.name: Hotel Golden Inca
voyage.content: Very quiet, beautiful rooms, clean and cozy.

voyage.name: Tierra Viva Cusco Centro
voyage.content: Upscale hotel with spacious, clean, well-appointed rooms with quality linens, good smelling soaps, bottled water. On-site restaurant serves a hearty buffet breakfast.

voyage.name: Tierra Viva Cusco Saphi
voyage.content: Many of the rooms on the second floor have high ceilings with white-painted wood beams visibly charming. The hotel is organized around two interior courtyards. Breakfast is included. The staff are attentive, speak great English, and can help you make reservations. The most interesting aspect of Tierra Viva Saphi is the location it is at the boundary between fancy Plaza de Armas and the poor hills around Cuzco it's ch

voyage.name: Palacio del Inka
voyage.content: The hotel was part of the Koricancha temple and during colonial times it became property of the conqueror Francisco Pizarro. Impressive interior with many paintings from the 17th century. Very good spread for breakfast. The hotel offers a daily, free, tour about the hotel and its history in the evenings.

voyage.name: Amerinka Boutique Hotel
voyage.content: Modern hotel that combines warm room atmospheres with professional and experienced attention. Near Plaza de Armas.

voyage.name: Hotel Monasterio
voyage.content: Housed in a former monastery, rooms are former monks' cells, but they are far from monastic. By far the most expensive place to stay in Cuzco. Avoid rooms 414-419, which are near a noisy generator.

voyage.name: Hotel Marqueses
voyage.content: The official hotel of SAS travel. Good staff and comfortable rooms. In the tourist district, 2 blocks from the Plaza des Armas.
